title: Greedy Best-First: Fast Paths in Glasgow Streets
description: Watch Greedy Best-First race across a real street-style graph, always expanding the node that looks closest to the goal. The result is a blazing-fast route that showcases how heuristic-driven search behaves on map graphs.
ig_caption:
🚦✨ **Greedy Best-First in Glasgow (Merchant City)**

In this visualization, the algorithm is guided by a *heuristic*—it prioritizes the next intersection that appears closest to the destination (based on an estimate like straight-line distance). 🧠📍

Under the hood, think of the street network as a **graph**: intersections are nodes, road segments are edges. Greedy Best-First uses a priority queue ordered by **h(n)** only (not the full cost-so-far), which often makes it feel *instant*—but it may choose locally promising routes that aren’t globally optimal. ⚡📉

💡 Tip: Because it ignores path cost accumulated so far (no g(n) term like A*), you’ll see it “lock on” to the goal direction—great for speed, sometimes not perfect for shortest paths.

👉 Want me to visualize the comparison vs **A*** on the same map next? Comment your pick! 👇
fb_caption:
🗺️ Algorithm spotlight: **Greedy Best-First** in Glasgow’s street-map graph!

We model real-world navigation as a graph search: intersections become nodes and roads become edges. Greedy Best-First always expands the node that *looks* nearest to the goal using a heuristic estimate—fast decisions, but not always the globally shortest route.
